claim: Dehydration and electrolyte imbalance cause an estimated 20% of heat-related workplace incidents in construction, mining, and agriculture.
EU occupational-health regulation on heat-stress duty of care is tightening.
The Meridian patch measures sweat electrolyte concentration and sweat rate continuously for up to 12 hours.
The dashboard flags workers trending toward dehydration 30-45 minutes before symptomatic decline.
Patch unit cost is EUR 3.80 at pilot volume with a target of EUR 1.10 at scale.
The ion-selective electrode array is printed rather than assembled, enabling roll-to-roll production.
Three patent families have been filed covering microfluidics, electrode printing, and alerting logic.
Bench validation against laboratory sweat analysis achieved r = 0.91 across 240 samples.
A field study with 62 participants across two summer construction seasons has been completed.
The field study was conducted jointly with the European Institute for Occupational Heat Safety and published in 2025.
The company has paid pilots with 5 industrial sites across two EU countries.
1,900 patches have been consumed in pilots to date with repeat orders from 4 of 5 sites.
There are 2.1M outdoor heat-exposed workers in Southern and Central Europe.
The CSO has published 14 papers on wearable sweat sensing.
Monthly burn is EUR 88k with 9 months of runway.
Positioning the product as occupational-safety equipment rather than a medical device materially lowers the regulatory burden.
Repeat orders from 4 of 5 pilot sites indicate genuine willingness to pay beyond pilot novelty.
A EUR 2.8M raise is appropriately sized for the stated manufacturing and validation milestones.
